claim: For the nearest-neighbor delayed Fisher–KPP lattice equation \(\dot u_n(t)=d(u_{n+1}(t)-2u_n(t)+u_{n-1}(t))+u_n(t-\tau)(1-u_n(t))\), with fixed \(d>0\) and unit growth coefficient, the minimal admissible positive wave speed \(c_\tau\) obeys \(\tau c_\tau^2/d=\log\tau+1+o(1)\) as \(\tau\to\infty\).
integrity: The claim is derived analytically from the published double-root characterization. One related 2006 lattice paper was accessible only through abstract and metadata; this is retained as an originality residual risk.
scientific_limitations: Fixed diffusion coefficient d>0 and unit delayed-growth coefficient only.
Nearest-neighbor lattice Laplacian and delayed logistic growth only; no added instantaneous death term or general spatial kernel.
The asymptotic gives the leading scale and additive constant but no next-order term or uniformity in d.
title: A logarithmic large-delay law for the minimal speed of a delayed Fisher–KPP lattice front
